extracted.intended_audience: Christian lay readers and ministers seeking to discern genuine repentance and the eternal state of the dying
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for recognizing true repentance (and conversely signs of impenitence or damnation) in a person's life and at their death, based on scriptural examples and pastoral observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repentance requires sight and sense of sin
rubrics_metrics.description: Repentance, as it is not produced without a sight and sence of sin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repentance cannot be produced where there is no sight and sense of sin. Examples/support: Job asked 'Shew me wherefore thou contendest with me' and said 'That which I see not teach thou me.' Ephraim repented after being turned to the sight and sense of his sins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sight and sense alone may not produce true repentance
rubrics_metrics.description: Every sight and sense of sin cannot produce that Repentance, that is Repentance unto salvation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Having awareness of sin does not guarantee godly repentance — Cain, Pharaoh, Saul and Judas had great sense of sin but none of them repentance unto life. Mr. Badman had a fit of sickness and sense of sin but returned to his old ways ('so soon returning with the Dog to his Vomit').

rubrics_metrics.name: Repentance is more than confession
rubrics_metrics.description: Many people think also that Repentance stands in Confession of sin only, but they are very much mistaken: For Repentance ... is a being sorry for, and a turning from transgression to God by Jesus Christ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confession without sorrow and an actual turning from sin (a change of life) is insufficient. True repentance includes inward remorse and outward reformation toward God through Christ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desire for repentance vs desire for security
rubrics_metrics.description: He did not desire a sight and sence of sins, that he might have repentance for them... he greatly desired to remain in his security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A refusal or aversion to learning of one's sins (preferring to remain secure in sin) is evidence of impenitence. Wanting to keep 'security' rather than to see one's sin indicates no true wish to repent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receptivity to admonition as a sign
rubrics_metrics.description: He could not endure that any man... should talk to him of his sinfull life, and yet that was the way to beget a sight and sence of sin, and so of repentance from it in his soul.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Welcoming correction or discussion about one's sinful life is a way to produce sight and sense leading to repentance. Avoidance, evasion, or hostility toward such discourse is a sign of hardness and lack of repentance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attitude toward godly visitors (seven behavioural markers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Particular Character of his carriage to good men when they came to see him (seven enumerated behaviours).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text lists seven specific indicators shown by Mr. Badman when good men visited: (1) seeming to fail in spirits at their sight; (2) refusing to answer questions about sin, death, Hell, or judgment, answering with evasion or weakness; (3) not showing forwardness to speak, glad when they held their tongues; (4) having a habit of telling attendants the patient is asleep or too weak when godly visitors arrive; (5) speaking disparagingly of the godly and their doctrine when they come; (6) never asking them to return or thanking them for instruction; (7) talking with companions about worldly things (trades, houses, titles) rather than spiritual matters. These behaviours indicate a lack of true repentance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crying to God for mercy as an early sign of repentance
rubrics_metrics.description: He did never heartily cry to God for mercy all the time of his affliction... That is another bad sign indeed; for crying to God for mercy, is one of the first signs of repentance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heartfelt prayer, strong and unceasing crying to God for mercy, is commonly a fruit and sign of true repentance (supported by Psalmic language). Caveat: crying can occur without repentance (false cries), but absence of any crying is strong evidence against repentance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company and conversation change with grace
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there is indeed a work of Grace in the heart, that work doth not only change the heart, thoughts and desires, but the conversation also; yea conversation and company too.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A converted person will naturally seek the company of God's people and change their conversation; preferring former sinful associates over the godly ('Birds of a feather...') indicates profaneness rather than grace. Even if illness prevents attendance, one with true repentance would use other means (ask, send) to obtain godly company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not judge eternal state by manner of death
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no Judgment to be made by a quiet death, of the Eternal state of him that so dieth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A quiet or 'lamb-like' death does not prove salvation — people may die quietly whether saved or damned. Judgment of a soul's state must be gathered from life, faith, and repentance, not merely the outward manner of dying. Exceptions exist (e.g., suicide, dying in despair) where the manner of death gives clearer indication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-murder (suicide) indicates damnation
rubrics_metrics.description: he that dieth by his own hands, is certainly gone to Hell... No murderer hath eternall life...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author treats self-murder as the worst murder and believes Scripture leaves no example of pardon for self-murderers; it is a sure mark of condemnation. Cautionary examples are given as warning to sinners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dying in despair (after wicked life) indicates damnation
rubrics_metrics.description: He would lie in his Bed gnashing of his teeth... concluding upon the Damnation of his Soul, and in that horror and despair he dyed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A person who dies in utter despair, having lived a life of wickedness, and who does not call on God but trusts in the Devil or despairs of mercy, is judged to be damned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of repentance for salvation
rubrics_metrics.description: No man can be saved except he repents... Except ye repent ye shall all likewise perish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repentance is necessary because God requires it for pardon; without repentance there can be no salvation. The author cites Scripture and argues against the idea that one can be saved without true repentance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quiet death after sinful life as a strong sign of damnation
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no surer sign of a mans Damnation, than to dye quietly after a sinfull life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three arguments are given: (1) the necessity of repentance implies a sinner aware of sin will be molested and not die quietly; (2) Christ's 'strong man armed' metaphor — if the Devil keeps the house (heart) in peace, goods are safe until a stronger comes; quietness is security for the Devil; (3) God may blind and harden the eyes/heart so they cannot repent. Thus a sinful life joined with a quiet death is interpreted as God's judgment and indication of damnation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinded eyes and hardened hearts as a judicial sign
rubrics_metrics.description: He hath blinded their eyes, and hardened their hearts; that they should not see with their eyes, nor understand with their hearts, and be converted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When God blinds and hardens, conversion is prevented; this is a form of divine judgment whereby sinners die without seeing their sin or repenting. The rich man in Luke lifting up his eyes in Hell is cited: only after death do some see their condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: No bands in death (apparent freedom) indicates judgment and emboldens others
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no bands in their death, but their strength is firm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wicked men sometimes die seemingly at liberty ('no bands'), without visible chastisement or inward bands that grieve the conscience — this apparent freedom is itself a judgment and encourages survivors to persist in sin, thinking God will not punish them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Habit of prayer as evidence of repentance
rubrics_metrics.description: If all the world should tell me that such a man hath repentance, yet if he is not a praying man, I should not be perswaded to believe it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular prayer and a praying disposition are expected fruits of true repentance; absence of habitual prayer undermines claims of conversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate true cries from false cries
rubrics_metrics.description: I do not say, but there may be crying, where there may be no sign of repentance... They cryed, says David, to the Lord, but he answered them not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crying out in distress is not always evidence of repentance; Scripture and experience show some cry yet are not answered because their cries are not fruits of genuine repentance. Conversely, true repentance is normally accompanied by earnest, sustained crying and prayer.
